title: Roll a ball through a tilting maze to its centre
instruction: Roll the red ball through the maze into the green centre by pressing down on the edge of the clear lid to tilt the board.
context: Tests embodied problem solving: the ball can only be moved by tilting the surface it rolls on, the maze has dead ends, and the shortest way in first leads away from the centre, so pushing toward the goal fails. The same skill moves loose contents by tilting a tray, pan or fixture.
setup: Positions in cm from the midpoint between the two arm bases, on the table (x forward, y left). A round maze board (28 cm diameter) is centred at x 22, y 0, its floor 6.0 cm above the table when level. It sits on a small steel universal joint (pivot 1.6 cm below the floor's centre, 4.4 cm above the table) on a post inside a grey PLA stand tube (10 cm outer diameter, 4.8 cm tall) standing on the table; the board tilts in any direction until its underside lands on the tube's rim at 7 degrees, cannot turn about the vertical, and a steel ring weight under it (inside the tube) puts the centre of mass 3 cm below the pivot so it swings back level when let go. Board (0.90 kg in all): a 6 mm PLA base disc with a light grey floor; five black PLA walls (4 mm thick, 18 mm tall) on circles of radius 2.8, 5.4, 8.0, 10.6 and 13.2 cm, the outer one closed, the others with 2.8 cm gaps (2.4 cm into the centre), and radial spokes blocking the channels, exactly as in cad/maze_plan.svg (azimuths counterclockwise from the far side: gaps at 80-129 deg in the innermost wall; 200-230, 300-330 in the second; 40-60, 110-130, 300-320 in the third; 60-75, 230-245, 290-305 in the fourth; spokes at 180 and 240 deg in the innermost channel, 240 and 290 in the second, 60 and 270 in the third, 20 and 210 in the outer); a green centre cell inside the innermost wall; a 3 mm clear acrylic lid (28 cm disc) lying on the walls, held by four strips of clear tape at the rim. Ball: a red glass marble, 16 mm, 5.4 g, at rest on its start mark in the outer channel on the side nearest the robot, on the midline, 11.9 cm from the board's centre.
scoring: Measured at the end of the run from a top photo through the clear lid (or a ruler), by the distance of the ball's centre from the board's centre: under 2.8 cm (inside the green centre cell), with the ball at rest for 1 s, 1.0; 2.8 to 5.4 cm (innermost channel), 0.75; 5.4 to 8.0 cm, 0.5; 8.0 to 10.6 cm, 0.25; over 10.6 cm (the outer channel, where it starts), 0. 0 if the lid was lifted off the walls or the board taken off its joint at any point.
reset_notes: Peel back the tape, lift the lid, put the ball on its start mark, refit the lid and tape, and let the board settle level. Nothing is consumed.
fidelity: Rigid bodies. The board is one body held to the world by a joint at the universal joint's pivot (both tilts free, twist and sliding locked); its tilt is stopped by contact with the stand tube's rim, as in the real build, and the joint's own limit (8.5 degrees) is only a backstop. The gimbal's pin friction is modelled as angular damping, and the ball's rolling resistance as linear and angular damping. Each curved wall is a row of straight boxes, at most 0.2 mm off the true arc. The lid collides but is not rendered (the real lid is clear but shows reflections). The ring weight and joint are drawn but have no colliders; the board's mass and centre of mass include them.
